What are your favorite WW2 movies/ TV series?

Saving Private Ryan would probably be my favorite WW2 movie, I loved the part where Tom Hanks character is shooting the tank with his pistol.

It's not a TV show or movie, but I also loved call of duty world at war. It did a pretty good job capturing parts of the war that weren't really covered by mainstream games up to that point.
Unsere mutern unsere vatern was an awesome miniseries. Watched it with a friend a couple weeks ago and was blown away by the quality of the series. Easily one of my top 5 tv shows ever.
I thought 'The Pacific' was really good. Saving Private Ryan was a great movie.

"Das Boot" is probably my favourite WW2 movie. It is about the life on the German submarine U-96 during the year 1941. The author of the book, Lothar-Guenther Buchheim, was a war correspondent and the story is based on his experiences during the war. The book is even better in my opinion. There is also a series based on the directors cut of the movie, which is about 5 hours long IIRC.
Came in here to say "Das Boot." When the crewmen cries, "We're sinking!" and it fades to black, my stomach just wrenches.
Letters From Iwo-Jima is a very good take on the battle of, well, Iwo-Jima.

If you want a good documentary, I'd suggest "The Greatest Story Never Told". It shows the story of world war two from the perspective of the Nazis. Of course, it has some obvious bias, but should undoubtedly be watched by anyone with any interest on the subject. It give any watcher a paradigm shift and works to dispel the post-war propaganda.

Of course, people will say something among the lines of "That's just neo-nazi propaganda". I'd like to say that the documentary is indeed well researched and should you be afraid of that, then you're already the subject of propaganda.

Other than that, I'd have to give credit to Band of Brothers. The Pacific was good too, but BoB was better. I also hear that Brad Pitts Fury is actually very accurate, despite being fiction. Haven't seen it yet but it's on my watchlist.

In that vein, I highly suggest Amazon's "The Man in the High Castle", a series based on the Phillip K. Dick novel.

You can watch the pilot episode for free!

Battle of Britain from 1969 has a special place in my heart. My grandfather was a vet, stationed in Britain for training during the blitz (he later participated in D-Day with the 1st Canadian Paratroop Battalion) and this film was the first one he took my father to see when he was a kid. It was a major bonding moment for them, and my grandfather loved the movie.

About three years before he died, a local independent theatre (which has since closed) showed the movie. He, my father, and I all went to see it.

So, yeah, a special movie for me.
